messages:
alex: Heads-up: nightly kernel harness picked up 3 candidate kernels with p99 regressions (~12-18%) on T4 for seqlen=1024. CI logs linked.
perf-bot: perf-ci triggered nightly-run/1801234600 — summary: k1 +18% p99, k2 +12% p99, k3 +2% (noisy). https://ci.redwood/1801234600
maria: I reproduced locally. k1 shows a big spike when bs=1 and seqlen>=1024. Reproducer: `./bin/kernel_bench --kernel k1 --arch ampere --seqlen 1024 --bs 1 --iters 500`
sam: I traced a few sample requests — KV-cache invalidation + extra loads on the matmul loop for k1. Flame graph suggests L2 miss storm.
jia: We should be careful: autotuner picks need to be sequence-length dependent. k1 might be fine for short paths (<256) but not for >512. We should store picks as (arch, seqlen_bucket) -> kernel.
alex: +1. Can we gate this in perf CI so next nightly only promotes kernels that pass seqlen-specific checks? Any quick config change?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out canary policy `seqlen_routing=dynamic` to staging at 1801234820. Will route seqlen>=512 to stable kernels by default.
maria: I also ran a focused microprobe: `scripts/run_microprobe.sh --kern k1 --probe cache-line --arch ampere` — result: L2 miss rate x3.4 vs baseline; cache-line stride looks suspicious.
sam: Proposal: add a microbenchmark matrix in CI that sweeps (seqlen:128,512,1024) x (bs:1,4,16) x (kv_hit_rate:0.0,0.5,0.9). That should catch layout-sensitive regressions for candidate kernels.
perf-bot: perf-ci: created job `perf/test-seqlen-kernels` with matrix [seqlen:128,512,1024] x [bs:1,4] — queued nightly
alex: Filing a regression ticket: ENG-kerbench-329 (kernel candidate p99 regressions for seqlen>=1024). @maria taking lead?
maria: I'll own it. Will dig into the matmul microcode path and post findings tomorrow. :eyes:
note: This thread is a short dev discussion tracking a nightly microbenchmark regression and the immediate operational mitigations. Messages are intentionally concise like typical Slack threads.
